single_nq_dev_5797
why do longer dna molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis
A: ["Gel electrophoresis", "Agarose gel electrophoresis"]
Q: why do longer dna molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis
A: "Longer DNA molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis because the gel matrix acts as a sieve. The pores in the gel are more easily traversed by shorter molecules, allowing them to migrate faster through the gel. In contrast, longer DNA molecules encounter more resistance as they navigate through the pores, which hinders their movement and results in slower migration. This phenomenon is known as sieving, where the size of the molecules affects their ability to move through the gel."
A: Longer DNA molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis because the gel matrix acts as a sieve. The pores in the gel are more easily traversed by shorter molecules, allowing them to migrate faster through the gel. In contrast, longer DNA molecules encounter more resistance as they navigate through the pores, which hinders their movement and results in slower migration. This phenomenon is known as sieving, where the size of the molecules affects their ability to move through the gel
